key_insight: Combines clustering-based risk stratification, synthetic data augmentation, and attention-guided offline reinforcement learning to produce interpretable, risk-aware sepsis treatment recommendations; attention scores provide per-patient feature/time importance for transparency.
problem_solved: Learning reliable, interpretable treatment policies from scarce, biased retrospective ICU data and heterogeneous patient presentations — enabling risk-tailored decision support without online experimentation.
method: Clustering-based stratification at ICU admission to assign patients into low / intermediate / high-risk cohorts with statistical validation.
Synthetic data augmentation to reduce class imbalance and expand coverage of treatment trajectories for offline learning.
Attention-based offline reinforcement learning that derives treatment policies from historical data while exposing attention weights for interpretable, patient-specific rationale.
impact: Provides a practical pipeline for AI/ML practitioners to build safer, more transparent sepsis decision-support models from electronic health records, improving trust and enabling targeted interventions by risk group.
visual_elements: Flowchart: patient admission → clustering → risk group → attention-RL policy → recommendation
Cluster scatter (UMAP/t‑SNE) colored by risk group with outcome/mortality overlay
Attention heatmap across time/features for example patients showing which signals drove each treatment recommendation
Bar/stacked chart of recommended actions and expected outcomes stratified by risk cohort (decision-dashboard mockup)
paper_title: Attention-Based Offline Reinforcement Learning and Clustering for Interpretable Sepsis Treatment
paper_authors: Punit Kumar, Vaibhav Saran, Divyesh Patel, Nitin Kulkarni, Alina Vereshchaka
